### Fixed
- **The managers take their login from muster's OAuth server block** (giantswarm/agent-platform#484): model-manager — on by default — failed on every installation that set `global.identity.issuerUrl` alone (`oauth.dex.clientSecret or oauth.existingSecret is required when oauth.enabled`, the child release's error), and a customer installation, whose muster logs in with its own Dex client, cannot take a fleet-wide `global.identity.clientId`. The meta chart now fills what a manager's `oauth` block and `global.identity` leave unset from `muster.muster.oauth.server` (`agent-platform.identity.apply`, on the shaped values, so the connectivity release sees the same blocks): for model-manager, agent-manager, vm-manager and cluster-manager `oauth.dex.issuerURL` (`dex.issuerUrl`), `oauth.dex.clientID` with `oauth.trustedAudiences: [<client>]` (`dex.clientId`, the charts' own default from `global.identity.clientId`) and `oauth.existingSecret` (`existingSecret`, key `dex-client-secret`), for the dex provider while muster's OAuth server is on; for the two routed managers `oauth.baseURL` `https://<route hostname><route.pathPrefix>` under an agentgateway-* `ingress.mode` (`modelManager.route.hostname` / `agentManager.route.hostname`, else `agentgateway.<global.domain>`). A manager's own value wins, and so does `global.identity` (nothing is filled then: the charts read it themselves). The connectivity chart's model-manager guard gains its absence checks back once the installation names its login (muster's OAuth server on with a Dex issuer): a missing issuer, client, secret or base URL fails the connectivity render naming the value to set; a render that names no login is untouched. `make verify-managers` asserts the four derivations, both winners, the one-login guard and the absence guard through the meta and connectivity renders. An installation that sets `global.identity` and the base URL explicitly renders byte-identically.
